reason: Logistics are feasible, but the plan as pre-registered is unlikely to produce a scored probe. Under the idea's own honest gate, the chance of a scored probe before 29 Sep 10:00 UTC is about 0.3-0.4, well below 0.7. (1) The numbers the idea cites are correct: out_full_P/report.txt gives kill test 1.4517 vs 1.2963 and 1.5699 vs 1.5668, all-peak z shift +0.567 vs -0.021, and leak5 OOF without x138-train 1.698 / 1.538 / 1.239. The whole train+eval run took 313.5 s on CPU on the user's Windows laptop, and the captures sit there, fetched from the Kaggle kernels vitaliineibauer/biohub-chcap-*. So the gate is cheap. (2) The gate is likely to fail. It needs P_matched M2 <= 0.98 x REPLICA-20 AND <= none on BOTH embryo directions. The existing numbers already show near-zero offset-free transfer. The value skeptic's per-axis debiased MAE for 44b6->6bba is P 2.072 vs none 2.079 (0.3%, with no 2% margin against a same-embryo replica). For 6bba->44b6, P debiased is 1.335 vs public 1.289, and public (in-embryo) is not gating, but REPLICA-20 on 6bba may land in the same range (research/wf_ideas_v3/v_redteam-past_head199-x138-two-arm_value.notes.md). I estimate P(gate pass) at ~0.35-0.45 (guess). With P(logistics) ~0.9 and P(user OK) ~0.9, P(scored) is ~0.3-0.4. (3) Two implementation defects in the plan as described. (a) x138's refine() raises RuntimeError when any |shift| > 2.00001 um (exp56 cell 4). Arm B's P - mean(P) + mean(public) can exceed 2 um, so the kernel would crash on the hidden test unless the result is re-bounded. (b) refine() only sees the frame's candidate array arr, not the 4.8M 'all peaks' sample. The lab mean-matching must be defined on the same per-frame arr, or the gate is not testing what ships. (4) Discriminability. The expected gain (+0.002) is below the LB noise quoted in BRIEF (~0.003 between byte-identical public notebooks). The adoption rule 'base + 0.001' would therefore largely select on noise, even if it scores.

Proceed only if Arm B passes. If it passes: (a) in the Arm B refine(), compute the per-frame means over the same arr the kernel sees, then rescale any shift with norm > 1.99 um back to 1.99 um before x138's 2 um assert. Add a dummy-run assert that counts re-bounded nodes (expect < 1%). (b) Use the identical per-frame kept-peak mean in the lab gate. (c) Add --patch headswap to build_probe_kernel.py --base x138: extra dataset source + replace the rglob 'biohub-v1284-head-s075/v1284_head.pt' anchor (it must stay a single match, or the kernel raises 'mount mismatch'). Headswap off must stay byte-identical to exp56, and headswap must compose with divinsert in case exp57b wins. (d) Ship ONLY Arm B: 1 slot, not 2, because a 2-arm A/B at +/-0.002 on a 0.003-noise LB cannot pick a winner. If the gate fails, stop (0 slots, 0 GPU); that is the pre-registered outcome.
realistic_public_gain: ~0 (-0.003 .. +0.004). Only the ~0.4-probability gate-pass branch reaches the LB, and there the gain is likely in the +0.000..+0.003 range, below LB noise.
